踝鈴不是手持樂器，初學時先將鈴串繫於腳踝上方，貼靠外踝與內踝。發聲來自舞者踏步、: Ankle bells are not a hand-held instrument. To begin, tie the string of bells above the ankle, resting against the outer and inner ankle bone. The sound comes from the dancer's steps, turns and foot rhythms, which make the small metal bells strike one another. Children can start with about fifty bells and add more as they grow older and more skilled. In Indian classical dance — Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kuchipudi, Mohiniyattam, Lavani and Odissi — they reinforce the rhythm and let a complex footwork be heard. Folk dancers in Nepal use nine to twenty-seven bells sewn onto a cloth strip tied at the ankle, choosing the number of bells to suit the song. There is also ankle-bell playing (ghunghroo vadan), which uses footwork as percussion and is performed in purely musical settings where dancing is not allowed.
踝鈴主要出現在印度古典舞蹈的節奏伴奏中，例如婆羅多舞、卡塔克舞、庫奇普迪舞、摩西: Ankle bells appear mainly in the rhythmic accompaniment of Indian classical dance, for example Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kuchipudi, Mohiniyattam, Lavani and Odissi; dancers tie strings of small bells above the ankle so that a complex footwork can be heard by the audience. Folk dance in Nepal uses similar ankle bells, choosing a version with more or fewer bells according to the song. There is also a form of ankle-bell playing developed by V. Anuradha Singh, performed as percussion with the feet at purely musical festivals where dancing is not allowed.
踝鈴主要由黃銅或鋼製成的小球形鈴鐺組成，每枚鈴鐺內置金屬珠球，振動時產生清脆聲響: Ankle bells consist mainly of small spherical bells made of brass or steel, each holding a metal bead inside that produces a clear ring when it vibrates. The bells are usually threaded onto a strap of cotton cloth or leather, which goes around the ankle and is fastened with ties. Better ankle bells are made of pure copper or brass, which gives a finer sound. The metal spheres are cast and polished with care so that the timbre stays clear. The cloth or leather strap uses a durable cotton-linen weave or soft leather, with a comfortable lining to protect the wearer's skin.
踝鈴起源於印度，是古老的舞蹈伴奏樂器，已有數千年的歷史。在印度古典舞蹈傳統中，踝: Ankle bells originated in India and are an old dance-accompaniment instrument with a history of several thousand years. In the Indian classical dance tradition they are called "Kathak" (ghungroo): dancers tie several dozen small bells around the ankle and produce strongly rhythmic ringing through their stamping steps. The instrument is inseparable from the art of Indian classical dance and plays an important role especially in Bharatanatyam and Kathak.
踝鈴音色清脆明亮，具有穿透力強的金屬質感。其音域範圍較窄，主要集中在高頻區域，能: Ankle bells have a clear, bright timbre with a strongly penetrating metallic quality. Their range is narrow and sits mainly in the high frequencies, producing a sharp, distinct sound. Because the principle is idiophonic, the sound comes straight from the resonance of the metal spheres; it decays naturally and is quick and short. Compared with the tambourine, ankle bells are higher and more strident; unlike the deep weight of bells and chimes, and unlike the single purity of the triangle, they carry many overtones with a light, springy pulse. When the wearer moves, several ankle bells together form a layered sound with a rich sense of timbral depth, especially suited to building a joyful, heated dance atmosphere.
踝鈴（ghungroo）是體鳴樂器，由許多小金屬鈴串結而成，綁在腳踝上方使用。印: Ankle bells (ghungroo) are an idiophone made of many small metal bells strung together and tied above the ankle. Indian classical dancers wear them in traditional performance, sounding them with the feet and emphasising the rhythm so that a complex footwork can be heard by the audience; a single string may hold fifty to more than two hundred bells. Folk dancers in Nepal also use similar ankle bells, called chap locally, usually nine to twenty-seven small bronze bells sewn onto cloth and tied at the ankle.
隨著文化交流，踝鈴逐漸傳播至中東、北非及東南亞地區，在民族舞蹈中廣泛應用。到了現: Through cultural exchange ankle bells gradually spread to the Middle East, North Africa and Southeast Asia, where they are widely used in folk dance. In modern times they have gone beyond any one region and become a familiar instrument in dance performance, yoga classes and folk music around the world. They keep their traditional cultural character while also meeting the needs of present-day performing arts.
